threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think paying for the tube is normal. Everyone else here rides their bike or takes the bus, even in the rain.
Heard a guy on the 36 last night arguing with his mate about whether pints or cocktails are better for a night out. Classic South London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw the three generations of my neighbor's family all arguing passionately over who makes the best kebab right on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a U-Bahn station that looks like a museum, with art installations and exhibitions right on the platform. It’s a trip before you even ride.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name at least three taco trucks that don’t even have a sign but still serve the best al pastor.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a full-sized grand piano at the Powell station last week. A crowd gathered, and for a brief moment, no one cared about the delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it’s really the small, tucked-away plazas where we gather that show our true spirit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they fumble with the metro card machines—standing there like lost tourists while locals swipe and dash.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just hopping on the Overground like a local—it’s a dead giveaway you’re fresh off the boat.
Last night on the 59, a bloke tried to convince everyone that pineapple on pizza is a crime. The driver just laughed and blasted the horn.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy playing the accordion at 3 AM outside my window while a group of friends debated the best kebab spots. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, showcasing local artists right alongside the döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their nonchalant reaction to BART delays. Tourists are still checking their watches; locals just grab a burrito and wait it out.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 at 16th and Mission yesterday, bus filled to the brim with folks in costume heading to a gig—mix of laughter and spilled coffee.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can stroll through Parc Güell and soak in the art, but miss the little murals tucked between the houses in Gràcia’s back alleys.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to sit at the bar when ordering a drink. Locals know that's where the real conversations happen.
